status_note: SUPERSEDED - historical record of the review round that produced CR-001, CR-002 and CR-003 against the branch as it stood at commit 92cc54ba0. Every statement below describes the code at that point, not the final implementation. All three findings are resolved, and three further MR-review items (MR-001 bounded AWS credential lookup with not_checked on an unresolvable chain, MR-002 missing[] reduced to configuration setting names only, MR-003 lifespan wiring test) are resolved on top of them; see code-review-check.json for the current verdict and the 'Deviations from this plan' section of plan.md for why the implementation departed from the plan. Notable differences from the text below: the result type is a tri-state ModelProviderStatus rather than a boolean; the LiteLLM and other-provider branches report not_checked rather than configured; the startup failure path reports not_checked with a sanitized reason and never interpolates exception text; and the AWS credential-chain resolution is bounded and acknowledged to possibly contact STS or metadata endpoints.
rationale: 3 blocking findings survive triage from a cross-lens cluster around startup crash-safety and a confirmed LiteLLM proxy-mode spec gap. CR-001 and CR-002 are unambiguous patches (no exception guard around the new startup check; healthcheck can 500 if app.state is unset outside the real lifespan-driven app). CR-003 is decision_needed: the acceptance lens independently flagged (status: fail) that the LiteLLM-proxy branch checks only is_litellm_enabled() and ignores LLM_PROXY_MODE, contradicting the ticket's own 'Notes and assumptions' spec text and this task's own technical-analysis.md Risk Indicator — but that simplification was an explicit user instruction given mid-session, so it needs human confirmation rather than a silent revert. 5 findings dismissed: a boto3 credential-chain docstring slightly overclaims 'no network call' (real but low-impact, scoped only to Bedrock deployments, boto3 already a core dependency so the separately-raised 'new hard dependency' concern is moot); reporting other (non-Azure/Bedrock) providers and the LiteLLM branch as configured without per-provider credential checks, and computing readiness once at startup without refresh, are explicitly spec'd design choices (ticket: 'a dial or gcp deployment is reported as configured rather than falsely flagged'; 'Compute the check result once at startup'), not defects.

business_review.item: AC10: operator supplies credentials for a single hosted provider (Azure OpenAI or AWS Bedrock) and configures nothing else -> app starts, chat works via that provider
business_review.notes: Diff does not touch the chat path; readiness check for Azure/Bedrock correctly derives provider from llm_service.get_default_model_for_category(GLOBAL) and validates the exact settings named in the spec.

business_review.item: AC10 Negative: no model provider configured -> app still starts and names the missing configuration, rather than silently presenting a working product that fails on first chat
business_review.notes: Native branches (no default model / Azure / Bedrock / unset provider) correctly warn and surface not_configured. The LiteLLM branch reports configured=True whenever is_litellm_enabled() is True (HAS_LITELLM and LLM_PROXY_ENABLED), never checking LLM_PROXY_MODE == 'lite_llm'; with LLM_PROXY_ENABLED=true and LLM_PROXY_MODE left at default 'internal', chat actually routes through the internal Azure/Bedrock path per llm_factory.py:1087,1141 — see CR-003.

business_review.item: "What configured means": MODELS_ENV selects a profile file that loads
business_review.notes: Explicitly out of scope per plan.md Global Constraints — YAML load happens at import time and a failure there already crashes the process before lifespan() runs.

business_review.item: "What configured means": profile contains >=1 enabled chat model, and a GLOBAL default model exists
business_review.notes: Reuses llm_service.get_default_model_for_category(ModelCategory.GLOBAL), which filters on model.enabled and is_default_for(GLOBAL).

business_review.item: "What configured means": Azure OpenAI credentials = AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY and AZURE_OPENAI_URL both present
business_review.notes: Implemented verbatim in the Azure branch, with dedicated tests for missing key, missing url, and both-present.

business_review.item: "What configured means": AWS Bedrock credentials = AWS_BEDROCK_REGION plus resolvable AWS credentials from the standard credential chain
business_review.notes: _check_aws_bedrock_configured() checks AWS_BEDROCK_REGION and delegates to _has_resolvable_aws_credentials() (boto3.Session().get_credentials(), local resolution).

business_review.item: A configuration that satisfies credentials but not the selected profile (e.g. AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY set while MODELS_ENV=aws) must be reported not configured, with the mismatch named
business_review.notes: Credential checks key off the selected profile's actual default_model.provider, not off which env vars are set; covered by test_models_env_aws_with_only_azure_credentials_reports_missing_bedrock_configuration.

business_review.item: Providers beyond Azure/Bedrock (dial default, gcp, google_vertexai, anthropic, vertex_ai-anthropic_models) must be reported configured, not falsely flagged
business_review.notes: Fallback branch returns configured=True for any non-Azure/non-Bedrock, non-None provider, matching the ticket's explicit note; tested.

business_review.item: LiteLLM proxy mode (LLM_PROXY_ENABLED=true AND LLM_PROXY_MODE=lite_llm) is reported as the configured provider without inspecting LiteLLM's own credentials
business_review.notes: Gates the proxy branch on is_litellm_enabled() alone, which does not check LLM_PROXY_MODE. technical-analysis.md's own Risk Indicators section already flagged this exact gap. See CR-003.

business_review.item: Global Constraint: never log or return secret values, only setting names
business_review.notes: log_model_provider_readiness() only interpolates provider/missing (setting names) and MODELS_ENV; healthcheck returns only {status, provider}. Explicitly tested.

business_review.item: Global Constraint: /healthcheck HTTP status code stays 200 in both configured and not-configured cases
business_review.notes: No status_code override; both new tests assert 200. See CR-002 for a robustness gap outside the real app-construction path.

business_review.item: Global Constraint: no outbound network call to Azure or AWS at startup — configuration/credential-chain presence only
business_review.notes: Azure branch only reads config; Bedrock branch uses local boto3 credential-chain resolution matching the get_bedrock_runtime_client() precedent.

business_review.item: Global Constraint: the check must not load or re-parse llm-<MODELS_ENV>-config.yaml itself
business_review.notes: Only calls llm_service.get_default_model_for_category(), reusing the already-loaded llm_config singleton.

business_review.item: Compute readiness once at boot, store on app.state, log INFO when configured / WARNING when not configured, surface on GET /healthcheck without blocking startup
business_review.notes: Wired via _check_model_provider_readiness(app) in lifespan(); healthcheck() reads app.state back. See CR-001 for the missing exception guard on the 'without blocking startup' half of this requirement.

standards_review.notes: All 5 commits use 'EPMCDME-14653: <Description>' matching .ai-run/guides/standards/git-workflow.md's <TICKET-ID>: Short Description convention.

License headers present on all new files (ruff/license-check would catch otherwise). New module uses typing.Optional[str] rather than the guide's preferred X | None — verified this is not ruff-enforced (pyproject.toml ruff select list has no UP rules) and is the prevailing convention across 20+ other src/codemie/service/*.py files, so not a blocking deviation.

Matches .ai-run/guides/development/security-patterns.md's secret-handling rule: only setting names are logged/returned, never values; explicitly unit-tested (test_log_model_provider_readiness_never_logs_a_credential_value). /healthcheck was already unauthenticated before this change; not a new auth regression.

findings.title: No exception guard around startup readiness check
findings.problem: _check_model_provider_readiness(app) calls check_model_provider_readiness() and log_model_provider_readiness() with no try/except; any unexpected exception from that call chain propagates straight out of lifespan() and aborts startup.
findings.impact: Directly threatens the ticket's central requirement that the app always starts, configured or not. A bug or edge case in this new diagnostic-only code path would produce the exact 'app doesn't start' failure the ticket exists to prevent — for logic whose entire job is informational, not correctness-critical.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the body of _check_model_provider_readiness in try/except Exception; on failure store a safe fallback ModelProviderReadiness(configured=False, provider=None, missing=[f'model provider readiness check failed: {exc}']) on app.state and log a WARNING instead of re-raising, so a bug in the diagnostic itself can never block startup.

findings.title: healthcheck() can 500 if app.state.model_provider_readiness is unset
findings.problem: request.app.state.model_provider_readiness is accessed with no default; any FastAPI app that mounts this router without running main.py's lifespan (e.g. a test harness, or future router reuse) raises AttributeError. This repo's own existing test_common.py / test_common_router.py already build a bare app = FastAPI(); app.include_router(router) for other endpoints in this same router.
findings.impact: Not reachable via the real production entrypoint (main.py:876 wires app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan), so app.state is always set before requests are served), but it turns a documented always-200 liveness probe into one that can 500 under non-standard app construction, undermining the ticket's explicit 'do not change /healthcheck's status-code semantics' constraint.
findings.recommendation: Use readiness = getattr(request.app.state, 'model_provider_readiness', None) and fall back to a safe default (e.g. status: 'unknown', provider: None) when None, so the probe can never fail regardless of how the app was constructed.

findings.title: LiteLLM proxy branch ignores LLM_PROXY_MODE, deviating from the ticket's own spec
findings.problem: check_model_provider_readiness() gates the LiteLLM-proxy branch on is_litellm_enabled() alone (HAS_LITELLM and config.LLM_PROXY_ENABLED), never checking config.LLM_PROXY_MODE == 'lite_llm'. The ticket's 'Notes and assumptions' section defines LiteLLM proxy mode as LLM_PROXY_ENABLED=true AND LLM_PROXY_MODE=lite_llm together, and this task's own technical-analysis.md documented this exact gap as a Risk Indicator, citing core/errors.py:800's three-part condition as the correct precedent. The simpler is_litellm_enabled()-only condition was substituted mid-session on explicit user instruction.
findings.impact: With LLM_PROXY_ENABLED=true and LLM_PROXY_MODE left at its default 'internal', llm_factory.py (lines 1087, 1141) actually routes chat through the internal Azure/Bedrock path, not LiteLLM — so an operator in that state with no Azure/Bedrock credentials gets a false 'configured, provider=litellm_proxy' from both the startup log and /healthcheck, then a first-message failure: precisely the outcome AC10 Negative requires the app to avoid. Currently untested — every LiteLLM-branch test monkeypatches is_litellm_enabled directly; none exercise LLM_PROXY_MODE.
findings.recommendation: Human decision needed: this diverges from the ticket's literal text on explicit user direction earlier in this session. Either (a) accept the narrower LLM_PROXY_ENABLED-only condition as an intentional scope reduction for this ticket, or (b) restore the config.LLM_PROXY_MODE == 'lite_llm' check (mirroring core/errors.py:800) to close the AC10 Negative gap — technical-analysis.md already has the exact precedent citation if (b) is chosen.
